rounds.text: Tech Mahindra commands an exceptional rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 with a BUY, Medium confidence rating [E63], backed by stellar recent operational velocity featuring 14% TTM sales growth [E17], a 27% surge in TTM compounded profit growth [E21], and net profit jumping 34% year-over-year [E66]. The company operates with pristine financial health, being almost debt-free [E59] with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x [E37] and generating robust free cash flow of Rs 5,626 Cr alongside full cash-backed profits at a 1.28x cash conversion rate [E34, E36]. Profitability metrics markedly outpace broader sector benchmarks, delivering an impressive 25.08% ROCE versus the 11.86% sector norm [E10] and an 11.42% ROA against a 5.9% benchmark [E8], while operating margins have expanded by 8 percentage points over three years to 17% [E30]. Conceded: [E45] and [E46] and [E70].

The valuation disconnect is severe, anchored by a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 724 per share against a trading price of Rs 1,779, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -145.8% [E45, E46]. Today's price trades at a rich P/E of 30.6 and a price-to-book of 5.87x, sitting right at its 52-week high with the stock at 100% of its range and 0.0% away from its peak [E1, E2, E48, E49, E70]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price already bakes in an aggressive 14.4% earnings growth expectation, which starkly contrasts with the base case assumption of just 2.0% growth [E47]. Beneath the buoyant near-term price momentum, historical growth has been sluggish, evidenced by a poor sales growth rate of 8.46% over the past five years and a meager 3-year compounded profit growth of only 1% [E19, E20, E61]. Institutional behavior reinforces these misgivings, with foreign institutional holdings dropping from 26.22% in September 2023 to 18.66% in June 2026, accompanied by an overall negative money flow signal [E42, E44]. Conceded: the company maintains a robust ROCE of 25.08%, excellent free cash flow of Rs 5,626 Cr, and an impressive trailing twelve-month profit growth of 27% [E10, E21, E36].

However, dismissing the stock's rich valuation metrics like a P/E of 30.6 and P/B of 5.87x ignores powerful fundamental outperformance, including a stellar ROCE of 25.08% and return on equity of 18.62% that dwarf sector benchmarks of 11.86% and 10.41% [E1, E2, E9, E10]. Furthermore, the bear's fixation on historical sluggishness overlooks explosive recent acceleration, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 27%, an operating cash flow of Rs 6,172 Cr, and free cash flow reaching Rs 5,626 Cr in March 2026 [E21, E35, E36]. Conceded: the reverse DCF implies 14.4% earnings growth against a 2.0% base case, but this aggressive expectation is fully supported by an active capex expansion phase with capital work-in-progress up 385.2% and a rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 confirming a buy rating on medium confidence [E40, E47, E63]. Finally, the stock's position at 100% of its 52-week range and its relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 reflect undeniable operational momentum, backed by a nearly debt-free balance sheet and a robust dividend payout of 112% [E48, E51, E59, E60].

However, citing these robust metrics ignores the stark reality that compounded sales growth over 3 years sits at a meager 2% and profit growth over 5 years is just 2% [E16, E19]. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 6,172 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 5,626 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. Yet, this operational cash generation is detached from the discounted cash flow model pinning intrinsic value at Rs 724 per share, resulting in a severe -145.8% margin of safety [E45, E46]. Conceded: capital work-in-progress is up 385.2% and the rules-based screen scores 88 out of 100 [E40, E63]. Nevertheless, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands an aggressive 14.4% earnings growth—far above the base case of 2.0%—creating a dangerous valuation blind-spot where the price fully prices in perfection [E47, E70]. Finally, pointing to a relative-strength rating of 100 and a price at its 52-week high disregards the persistent institutional flight evident in foreign holdings dropping from 26.22% to 18.66% and negative money flow [E42, E44, E48, E51].

Conceded: compounded 3-year sales growth is 2% and 5-year profit growth is 2% [E16, E19]. Conceded: intrinsic value from the DCF is Rs 724 and institutional holdings dropped from 26.22% to 18.66% [E42, E45]. However, focusing purely on historical growth ignores the explosive momentum in the trailing twelve months, where sales grew 14% and profit jumped 27% [E17, E21]. Furthermore, treating the DCF model as absolute truth dismisses the actual financial health of the firm, which boasts a stellar ROCE of 25.08% and an exceptional rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 [E10, E63]. The massive 385.2% surge in capital work-in-progress demonstrates an aggressive growth spend underway that will fuel future expansions, rendering past stagnations irrelevant [E40]. Finally, pointing to foreign institutional outflows overlooks the strong accumulation by domestic institutions, whose holdings rose from 27.03% to 36.92% [E43].

Conceded: sales grew 14% and profit jumped 27% in the trailing twelve months [E17, E21], and domestic institutional holdings rose from 27.03% to 36.92% [E43]. However, citing short-term trailing spikes glosses over the structural multi-year stagnation where 3-year compounded sales growth is a meager 2% and 5-year profit growth sits at 2% [E16, E19]. Dismissing the DCF model ignores its core warning that today's market price of Rs 1,779 demands a steep margin of safety deficit of -145.8% against an intrinsic value of Rs 724 [E45, E46]. The aggressive capital work-in-progress surge of 385.2% signifies an unproven capex build-up phase that carries execution risk rather than guaranteed expansion [E40]. Furthermore, foreign institutions have reduced their stake significantly from 26.22% to 18.66%, resulting in an overall negative institutional money flow signal [E42, E44]. Finally, leaning on a high ROCE does not excuse paying a rich valuation of 30.6x P/E and 5.87x price-to-book that already prices in perfection [E1, E2, E10].
